whyItPrints: QuickBooks Desktop still wants the old connector. People pay monthly per company file so an app can read and write it.
whyThisMatters:
Developers use Conductor to read and write QuickBooks Desktop and Enterprise from their own app. You get Python, Node or TypeScript, and a REST API. They count 256 typed endpoints. Create an invoice, fetch a customer, update a line. QuickBooks itself still wants the Web Connector, qbXML, and SOAP. Conductor hides that.

Your user connects their own company file. Guides cover the usual Windows and QuickBooks errors. A cryptic failure comes back as one error, with a plain fix. A dashboard is where you add connections and debug them. The end user does the hookup, so you aren't on that ticket. Testing is free for one connection. Production is a monthly price per company file. A lot of files moves you to enterprise pricing.

Conductor Labs is in San Francisco. They say it's syncing more than 1,600 businesses. Ramp shows up in a customer quote. Others mention leaving DBSync or Commercient, or retiring an XML bridge they had built themselves. You pay so the accounting file behaves like a normal API.
